The Media Line Staff

08/21/2026

# Trump warns of 'economic D-Day' against Iran, but Tehran is well acquainted with sanctions

## The Trump administration is touting a crushing financial campaign against Iran

The Trump administration is touting a crushing financial campaign against Iran. It's promising an “economic D-Day” against a country that has so far withstood nearly five decades of punishing American sanctions. President Donald Trump says the U.S. is imposing an “unprecedented” level of economic warfare and isolation on Iran, aiming to force its leadership to cave to demands to end its nuclear program and fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz to oil and natural gas tankers. As part of the next phase of the administration’s “Operation Economic Fury,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has threatened secondary sanctions on nations and companies that conduct business with Iran.

Russia and Ukraine together account for roughly a quarter of global grain exports. They reportedly exported nearly 100 million metric tonnes of grain in the year through June, but repeated attacks on Black Sea ports and vessels are increasingly disrupting the movement of agricultural commodities.

***In the face of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, the EU, together with Ukraine and Moldova launched the EU-Ukraine [Solidarity Lanes](https://transport.ec.europa.eu/ukraine/eu-ukraine-solidarity-lanes_en) in May 2022, establishing new transport routes to keep Ukraine’s imports and exports flowing via rail, road and inland waterways. Today, the EU-Ukraine Solidarity Lanes have become a lifeline for Ukraine’s economy.***

In July 2026 the Solidarity Lanes allowed:

* Around **90%** of Ukrainian imports (in comparison to around 10% through the Black Sea)
* Around **95%** of Ukrainian exports of non-agricultural products (in comparison to around 5% through the Black Sea)
* Around **20%** of Ukrainian exports of grain, oilseeds and related products (in comparison to around 80% through the Black Sea)
